question: A student travels to school by bus, bicycle or on foot with probabilities $\frac12$, $\frac3{10}$ and $\frac15$ respectively. The probabilities that the student reaches school late by these three modes are $\frac1{10}$, $\frac15$ and $\frac14$ respectively. Find the probability that the student reaches school late.
explanation:
Step 1: Identification of events
Let $B$, $C$ and $F$ denote the events that the student travels by bus, bicycle and on foot respectively. Let $L$ denote the event that the student reaches school late.
Step 2: Given probabilities
$$P(B)=\frac12,\quad P(C)=\frac3{10},\quad P(F)=\frac15$$ and $$P(L|B)=\frac1{10},\quad P(L|C)=\frac15,\quad P(L|F)=\frac14.$$
Step 3: Application of total probability
Since $B$, $C$ and $F$ form a partition of the sample space, $$P(L)=P(B)P(L|B)+P(C)P(L|C)+P(F)P(L|F).$$
Step 4: Substitution and simplification
$$P(L)=\frac12\times\frac1{10}+\frac3{10}\times\frac15+\frac15\times\frac14$$ $$=\frac1{20}+\frac3{50}+\frac1{20}=\frac4{25}.$$
Step 5: Conclusion
Hence, the probability that the student reaches school late is $$\boxed{\frac4{25}}.$$
